description: The complete LLM intelligence layer: weekly household digest, monthly close report, on-demand analysis, and what-if forecasting. All server-side OpenAI API calls with results cached to magic_actions_log. This turns raw financial data into actionable household intelligence.

timing.gatingCondition: Features 4 + 5 complete — budget data, rolling averages, and anomaly detection all feeding the LLM context.

principles: LLM adds color and insight — never replaces the raw data
Cache aggressively — same question with same data should not re-call the API
Degrade gracefully — if OpenAI API is down, app still works, just without narratives

SECRETS INVARIANT — all LLM prompts pass through secrets-guard sanitization. Only derived/aggregated data reaches the LLM: category names, amounts, date ranges, first names. Never access tokens, account numbers, .env values, or items table secrets. Enforced by test suite.
Forecasting is directional, not precise — communicate uncertainty clearly

techStack.testing: Jest for prompt construction, response parsing, caching logic

userStories.title: Weekly household digest
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduled job: Sunday evening (configurable cron expression)
Context assembled: week's cash flow, top spending categories vs. budget, active anomalies
LLM generates narrative: what happened this week, what's notable, one recommendation
Cached in magic_actions_log with type='weekly_digest' and period date
Displayed on dashboard in a 'Weekly Pulse' panel
Historical digests browsable (last 4 weeks)
userStories.testStrategy: Context assembly unit test (verify correct data selection). Prompt construction test (no PII). Cache hit/miss test. Mock LLM response rendering.

userStories.title: Monthly close report
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduled job: 1st of month, covers prior month
Content: budget vs. actual by category, notable wins/overruns, comparison to prior month and rolling average, net cash flow vs. income
LLM narrative: conversational summary of the month's financial health
Cached with type='monthly_close' and period
Displayed in a dedicated 'Monthly Report' section
Historical reports browsable
userStories.testStrategy: Context assembly test with known budget/actual data. Prompt completeness test. Cache key uniqueness test.

userStories.title: On-demand analysis
acceptanceCriteria: UI: text input or preset question buttons on dashboard
Preset questions: 'Explain this month\'s dining spend', 'What\'s our biggest discretionary category this quarter?', 'Are we on track for our savings goal?'
Free-form text input for custom questions
System assembles relevant financial context based on question intent
Response displayed inline on dashboard
Cached by prompt hash — same question with same underlying data returns cached response
Rate limiting: max 10 on-demand queries per day
userStories.testStrategy: Prompt hash generation test. Cache hit test. Rate limit test. Context assembly for different question types.

userStories.title: What-if forecasting
acceptanceCriteria: UI: text input for scenario questions
Examples: 'If we take a $6,000 trip in October, what does cash flow look like?', 'If Jordan starts at [university] at $X/semester in fall 2028, when do we redirect cash flow?'
System injects current financial snapshot: balances, monthly income, monthly expenses, savings rate
LLM generates projected impact with clear uncertainty caveats
Response includes: current state, projected impact, months until recovered/affected
Cached with scenario hash
userStories.testStrategy: Financial snapshot assembly test. Prompt security test. Uncertainty caveat presence test (response must include hedging language).

high: Prompt injection via free-form text input — must sanitize user input before including in LLM prompts
Secrets leaking to LLM — all prompt construction uses secrets-guard; test suite scans constructed prompts for known secret patterns (token prefixes, account number formats, env var values)
Financial advice liability — responses must clearly state they are informational, not financial advice
medium: OpenAI API cost — cache hit rate critical, monitor token usage
LLM hallucination about financial data — responses should reference actual numbers from context, not fabricate
API rate limits during digest generation for all family members
low: Tone consistency across different Magic Action types — may need per-type system prompts

preFlightChecklist: Confirm OpenAI API pricing for gpt-5-nano and set monthly budget cap
Design system prompts for each Magic Action type
Decide: disclaimer text for AI-generated financial analysis
Decide: should what-if forecasting be available to kids, or adults only?
